issue_context.title: Systemd 255~rc3 Journal failure ' Assertion 'left < right' failed ' when debugging enabled (sleep state changes)
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

systemd-255~rc3-1.fc40.src.rpm

### Used distribution

Fedora Rawhide (F40)

### Linux kernel version used

6.7.0amdfw-rc2+

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

systemd, systemd-journald

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

Journal should continue to function as normal (regression from 255-rc2).



### Unexpected behaviour you saw

after upgraded package from rawhide of 255-rc3 was pushed on the 25/11/2023 several debugging scripts now fail. Appears to be related to enabling several debug outputs at once. systemd fails to return state correctly to the debug script and then keeps temporary debug output enabled and spams the journal.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Was conducted using the following debug script which is designed to test s2idle state on amd platforms 

https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/drm/amd/-/blob/master/scripts/amd_s2idle.py

This script works fine preceding the -rc3 updates and now segfaults with the newer version of systemd. A separate bug was filled initially on the tracker here:

https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/drm/amd/-/issues/3012



### Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue

Could you provide the .journal file(s) that triggers the assertion?
Could you advise how and where to obtain these?

Just a comment this issue persisted when reverting to older / known stable kernels. Initially I had thought it was something to do with the patchset I was running trying  to debug unrelated issues with amd-pstate, but the bug followed. This was encountered on my daily driver so I have since moved to a non rawhide release. I'll need to reinstall rawhide to trigger the bug again if you need additional debug output. The linked bug initially filed includes additional output/logs.

> Could you advise how and where to obtain these?

You can find .journal files under /var/log/journal/MACHINE_ID/ or /run/systemd/journal/.
If the journal contains some private data you want not to make public, then please save the journals e.g. google drive or so, and send me a link.

review_comments: Why only do this logic if we're going in the down direction? Doesn't this apply regardless of the direction we're going in?
As 'left' is always tested when we are going to upwards. I extended the comment in the code.
